news.title: The Club World Cup deals the knockout blow to Infantino
news.lede: Aleksander Ceferin, president of European football's governing body (UEFA), and Nasser Al-Khelaifi, chairman of the European Club Association, are holding an anticipated meeting in the city of Salzburg. Tension is rising between their organisations and world football's governing body (FIFA), specifically against its president Gianni Infantino. According to the "talkSPORT" network, the root of that tension lies in the possibility of the European clubs withdrawing from the 2029 Club World Cup, following UEFA's decision regarding the national teams in relation to the World Cup. Spanish newspaper "AS" reported that there is as yet no agreement between the European Club Association and FIFA to stage the 2029 Club World Cup, which makes talk of boycotting the tournament inaccurate for now.

news.title: England Under-20s World Cup: Teenager Erica Meg Parkinson named in preparatory squad
news.lede: Erica Meg Parkinson joined US side North Carolina Courage at the start of July. Teenager Erica Meg Parkinson has been named in England's preparation squad for the Under-20 Women's World Cup in Poland next month. Boss Lydia Bedford has called up the North Carolina Courage midfielder, 18, as part of a 24-player squad for a warm weather training camp in Portugal next week. They will have a final opportunity to impress when they face their hosts in a friendly on Thursday, 13 August.

news.title: Figo demands Infantino’s exit over FIFA World Cup controversy
news.lede: Former Portugal captain Luis Figo has called for FIFA president Gianni Infantino to resign, describing him as “deceitful” as pressure continues to mount over the failed plan to sell a stake in the World Cup. The former Real Madrid and Barcelona star said Infantino had lost the moral authority to lead world football after abandoning the controversial proposal following widespread opposition. Infantino had sought to sell a 20 per cent stake in the World Cup through FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a private investment vehicle created to manage the commercial and operational aspects of FIFA tournaments. The proposal drew fierce criticism from football stakeholders and was rejected by three continental confederations, forcing FIFA to withdraw the plan.

news.title: Infantino breaks cover to arrive for crisis talks after World Cup plot failed
news.lede: DISGRACED Fifa president Gianni Infantino has broken cover to attend an emergency meeting in Morocco. A Mercedes containing the beleaguered supremo was seen swooping into Fifa’s African base in Rabat. It’s the first time Infantino has been spotted since his disgraceful plot to sell a stake in Fifa tournaments including the World Cup came to light. The usually attention-seeking honcho is facing total crisis, with the Fifa chief losing support by the day.

news.title: Oliver Baumann says Julian Nagelsmann apologized after World Cup benching
news.lede: Germany goalkeeper Oliver Baumann has opened up about one of the toughest moments of his career after Julian Nagelsmann opted to restore Manuel Neuer as the starting goalkeeper for the World Cup. Baumann had established himself as Germany’s No. 1 leading up to the tournament, but Nagelsmann, leaning on input from some key players, ultimately turned back to Neuer for football’s biggest stage. While the decision was undoubtedly disappointing for Baumann, the goalkeeper sayid that the ex-Germany coach, who was recently replaced by Jürgen Klopp, reached out afterward to discuss everything openly. “He [Nagelsmann] was sorry about how everything turned out in the end.

news.title: 'I'm not having this' - Jamie Carragher reveals he DECLINED FIFA World Cup request
news.lede: Jamie Carragher declined FIFA's request to publicly endorse the idea of staging the World Cup every two years instead of the customary four, following a confidential meeting. The Liverpool icon revealed he had met with former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, now FIFA’s chief of global football development along with several ex‑players to discuss the proposed restructure. This summer's tournament was held across the United States, Canada and Mexico, with European champions Spain lifting the trophy for the first time in 16 years. Luis de la Fuente's side beat Argentina 1-0 in the final at the New York New Jersey Stadium, with Ferran Torres scoring the winner.
